votes.evidence:
Doc claim (worktree products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:82-84): "Bot-authored PRs are refused at every layer — the webhook pre-filter (`_review_skip_reason`), the engine (`review_pr.py::_refuse_bot_author`, mirrored by `review_local.py`), and the Action's job gates", and AGENTS.md:89-91 names "dependabot/renovate/posthog-bot" as staying "refused everywhere".

Pre-filter definition (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:124-127): `_is_bot_authored` returns `user.get("type") == "Bot" or "[bot]" in login`. `_review_skip_reason` (tasks.py:218-233) returns "bot_author" only via that helper; the only other pre-filter is `author_association not in PAYLOAD_GATE_AUTHOR_ASSOCIATIONS` (tasks.py:98: TRUSTED | {"CONTRIBUTOR"}), which a real org-member machine user passes. So a `posthog-bot` (type "User", no "[bot]") PR is not refused by the webhook pre-filter; it proceeds toward the sandbox.

Engine definition (tools/pr-approval-agent/github.py:62-64, 79-89): `_BOT_MACHINE_USERS = {"posthog-bot"}`; `is_bot_author` matches type Bot, "[bot]" login, OR login in `_BOT_MACHINE_USERS`. That is what the engine gates on: review_local.py:207 sets `author_is_bot=is_bot_author(user)`, review_pr.py:224-226 refuses via `_refuse_bot_author` when `author_is_bot and not self_driving`. test_github.py:191 pins the machine-user case. The Action gate likewise checks `login != 'posthog-bot'` explicitly (.github/workflows/pr-approval-agent.yml:30, 255).

Net: for the machine-user login the doc names, the pre-filter layer does not refuse; only the engine (hosted path) and the Action gate do. The sentence at AGENTS.md:82-83 overstates the pre-filter's scope, in a section whose stated purpose is to be the contract future agents hold code to. No test in products/stamphog/backend/tests covers a posthog-bot payload at the pre-filter (grep found only "[bot]"/type-Bot cases). The `_is_bot_authored` helper is unchanged from master (main repo master tasks.py:149-152), so runtime behavior is pre-existing and safe; the defect is doc precision only.
votes.refutation: Tried: (1) Does the pre-filter refuse posthog-bot through another check? No — the only other payload gate is author_association, which an org-member machine user satisfies (tasks.py:98, 232). (2) Is "Bot-authored" in the doc scoped to the pre-filter's own definition so the sentence is trivially true? No — the same section explicitly lists posthog-bot among logins "refused everywhere", and the doc names three layers including the pre-filter. (3) Does the following bullet ("`is_bot_author` must not be weakened") already make the engine's wider scope clear? Partly, but it does not say the pre-filter is narrower, so a reader still believes two hosted layers cover machine users when only one does. (4) Is there any runtime consequence? None — engine and Action both refuse posthog-bot, so this is documentation accuracy only, hence `consider` rather than should_fix.

votes.refutation: Attempted refutation: the pre-filter's own docstring (tasks.py:219-223) frames it as "only the early-out" with the engine keeping "the same bot/draft refusals as defense in depth", and AGENTS.md:89-91 already tells agents `is_bot_author` "must not be weakened" and that posthog-bot stays refused everywhere; so the doc's overall outcome claim (posthog-bot is refused) is true and the engine layer is the documented authority. That narrows the harm to a doc wording issue with no runtime consequence, but it does not refute the specific claim: "refused at every layer — the webhook pre-filter" is factually false for machine-user logins, and the tasks.py:222 phrase "the same bot refusals" repeats the same imprecision rather than correcting it. votes.evidence:
The doc claim and both bot definitions check out exactly as the finding describes, and the trigger is reachable in production.

- /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:82-83 states: "Bot-authored PRs are refused at every layer — the webhook pre-filter (`_review_skip_reason`), the engine (`review_pr.py::_refuse_bot_author` ...), and the Action's job gates". Line 87-88 of the same section then names "dependabot/renovate/posthog-bot" as authors that "stay refused everywhere", so the doc's own definition of "bot" includes the posthog-bot machine user.
- /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:124-127 `_is_bot_authored` matches only `user.type == "Bot"` or `"[bot]" in login`. `_review_skip_reason` (tasks.py:229-231) returns "bot_author" only on that match. There is no other reference to posthog-bot or a machine-user set anywhere in products/stamphog/backend (grep: only tasks.py:124/157/169/229).
- /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/tools/pr-approval-agent/github.py:64 `_BOT_MACHINE_USERS = {"posthog-bot"}` and github.py:79-89 `is_bot_author` additionally matches `login in _BOT_MACHINE_USERS`. The Action gate also explicitly excludes it: .github/workflows/pr-approval-agent.yml:28-30 and 253-255 (`user.login != 'posthog-bot'`).
- Production reachability: posthog-bot is a real org member (type "User", no "[bot]" suffix), so its PRs carry `author_association` MEMBER, which is in `PAYLOAD_GATE_AUTHOR_ASSOCIATIONS` (tasks.py:98), and the write-permission gate (`_author_lacks_write_permission`, tasks.py:236+) does not refuse a machine user with push access. A posthog-bot-authored PR therefore passes the webhook pre-filter, burns a sandbox run, and is refused only inside the engine and by the Action gate. So of the three layers the doc lists, only two cover machine users.

Consequence is bounded: no security gap (engine + Action still refuse), just a wasted sandbox run and an inaccurate statement in the file whose stated purpose is to be the contract future agents hold code to. A one-clause qualification fixes it, which is why "consider" (not should_fix) is the right severity.
votes.refutation:
Attempted refutations:
1. "The pre-filter is only an early-out for cost, so 'refused' is loose language and harmless." The docstring at tasks.py:220-224 does say the pre-filter is "only the early-out" with the engine as defense in depth, but AGENTS.md:82-83 explicitly lists it as a refusal layer and the next bullet (87-88) names posthog-bot as refused "everywhere". A reader of AGENTS.md alone gets the wrong scope.
2. "posthog-bot PRs are refused by another webhook-side gate before the sandbox." Checked: `PAYLOAD_GATE_AUTHOR_ASSOCIATIONS` includes MEMBER (tasks.py:98), and no stamphog backend code references posthog-bot or a machine-user list. No such gate exists.
3. "posthog-bot never authors PRs in production." It is a real org machine user the engine and Action gate both special-case (github.py:64, pr-approval-agent.yml:30/255), which exists precisely because it does author PRs.
4. "The gap is already covered so it doesn't matter." True for runtime safety, which is why this is not should_fix, but the finding is about the accuracy of an agent-facing contract doc added by this PR, and that inaccuracy stands.
Refutation fails; the finding is real at consider severity.
